types.intro: A PLAN. Exactly four chapters in this order and nothing else: no extra headings, remarks, test output or status reports. The files of the Change hold the detail; discussion is kept outside this body.

chapters.name: Change
chapters.guidance: One line, `<id> <name>: <short description>`: the stable id, the name and what the Change is about. Do not repeat From, To or Because here.

chapters.name: Because
chapters.guidance: X, the value delivered, briefly. The value, not who asked for it.

types.intro: A DO. Exactly three chapters in this order and nothing else: no extra headings, remarks, test results, check status or execution logs. The Change, the Cases, the diff and the checks hold the evidence; discussion is kept outside this body.

chapters.name: Change
chapters.guidance: One line, `<id> <name>: <short description>`: the stable id, the name and the scope of this DO.

chapters.name: Implement
chapters.guidance: The behavior or functionality this DO intends to deliver, briefly.

chapters.name: Refactor
chapters.guidance: The improvement intended while behavior stays as it is, briefly. If no refactoring is planned, say so.

types.intro: An ACT. Exactly two chapters in this order and nothing else: no extra headings, retrospective text, test output or status reports. The files of the Change hold the detail; discussion is kept outside this body.

chapters.name: Change
chapters.guidance: One line, `<id> <name>: <short description>`: the stable id, the name and what the Change is about.

chapters.name: Records
chapters.guidance: What this ACT adds to the Change, named and not repeated. Today that is the 4L retrospective; it is a hint, not a closed list.

types.visible: **Change envelope.** The evidence is in the repository files of the Change(s) named below, at the revision under review.
types.intro: A HOTFIX. Exactly four chapters in this order and nothing else: no extra headings, remarks, test results, check status or execution logs. The Change, the Cases, the diff and the checks hold everything else; discussion is kept outside this body.

chapters.name: Change
chapters.guidance: One line, `<id> <name>`: the stable id and the name of the Change. An identity, not a description; the Defect says what is broken.

chapters.name: Defect
chapters.guidance: The Defect, by its identity `<capability>/D<n>`; a ticket number or URL is not that identity. What is broken, and which state is defective: production (the package and its published version), main, or a collector. They are different states; name the one you mean and claim no production impact that does not exist.

chapters.name: Urgency
chapters.guidance: Why this cannot follow the ordinary Change path, and the consequence of waiting. A ticket number or a priority label is not an answer.

chapters.name: Approach
chapters.guidance: Why this is the fastest safe path from the RED Case to GREEN, not a broader improvement or a refactoring: the choice and what it trades off, not the implementation. If production is affected, say what else from main a new published version would carry.
